69:   localparam int unsigned IdCounterWidth = cf_math_pkg::idx_width(MaxTrans);

296:     // control of the AR handshake
297:     always_comb begin
298:       // AXI Handshakes
299:       slv_resp_o.ar_ready    = 1'b0;
300:       ar_valid        = 1'b0;
301:       // `lock_ar_valid`: Used to be protocol conform as it is not allowed to deassert `ar_valid`
302:       // if there was no corresponding `ar_ready`. There is the possibility that an injection
303:       // of a R response from an `atop` from the AW channel can change the occupied flag of the
304:       // `i_ar_id_counter`, even if it was previously empty. This FF prevents the deassertion.
305:       lock_ar_valid_d = lock_ar_valid_q;
306:       load_ar_lock    = 1'b0;
307:       // AR id counter
308:       ar_push         = 1'b0;
309:       // The process had an arbitration decision in a previous cycle, the valid is locked,
310:       // wait for the AR transaction.
311:       if (lock_ar_valid_q) begin
312:         ar_valid = 1'b1;
313:         // transaction
314:         if (ar_ready) begin
315:           slv_resp_o.ar_ready    = 1'b1;
316:           ar_push         = 1'b1;
317:           lock_ar_valid_d = 1'b0;
318:           load_ar_lock    = 1'b1;
319:         end
320:       end else begin
321:         // The process can start handling AR transaction if `i_ar_id_counter` has space.
322:         if (!ar_id_cnt_full) begin
323:           // There is a valid AR, so look the ID up.
324:           if (slv_req_i.ar_valid && (!ar_select_occupied ||
325:              (slv_ar_select_i == lookup_ar_select))) begin
326:             // connect the AR handshake
327:             ar_valid     = 1'b1;
328:             // on transaction
329:             if (ar_ready) begin
330:               slv_resp_o.ar_ready = 1'b1;
331:               ar_push      = 1'b1;
332:             // no transaction this cycle, lock the valid decision!
333:             end else begin
334:               lock_ar_valid_d = 1'b1;
335:               load_ar_lock    = 1'b1;
336:             end
337:           end
338:         end
339:       end
340:     end
341: 
342:     // this ff is needed so that ar does not get de-asserted if an atop gets injected
343:     `FFLARN(lock_ar_valid_q, lock_ar_valid_d, load_ar_lock, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
344: 
345:     if (UniqueIds) begin : gen_unique_ids_ar
346:       // If the `UniqueIds` parameter is set, each read transaction has an ID that is unique among
347:       // all in-flight read transactions, or all read transactions with a given ID target the same
348:       // master port as all read transactions with the same ID, or both.  This means that the
349:       // signals that are driven by the ID counters if this parameter is not set can instead be
350:       // derived from existing signals.  The ID counters can therefore be omitted.
351:       assign lookup_ar_select = slv_ar_select_i;
352:       assign ar_select_occupied = 1'b0;
353:       assign ar_id_cnt_full = 1'b0;
354:     end else begin : gen_ar_id_counter
355:       axi_demux_id_counters #(
356:         .AxiIdBits         ( AxiLookBits    ),
357:         .CounterWidth      ( IdCounterWidth ),
358:         .mst_port_select_t ( select_t       )
359:       ) i_ar_id_counter (
360:         .clk_i                        ( clk_i                                       ),
361:         .rst_ni                       ( rst_ni                                      ),
362:         .lookup_axi_id_i              ( slv_req_i.ar.id[0+:AxiLookBits]             ),
363:         .lookup_mst_select_o          ( lookup_ar_select                            ),
364:         .lookup_mst_select_occupied_o ( ar_select_occupied                          ),
365:         .full_o                       ( ar_id_cnt_full                              ),
366:         .inject_axi_id_i              ( slv_req_i.aw.id[0+:AxiLookBits]             ),
367:         .inject_i                     ( atop_inject                                 ),
368:         .push_axi_id_i                ( slv_req_i.ar.id[0+:AxiLookBits]             ),
369:         .push_mst_select_i            ( slv_ar_select_i                             ),
370:         .push_i                       ( ar_push                                     ),
371:         .pop_axi_id_i                 ( slv_resp_o.r.id[0+:AxiLookBits]               ),
372:         .pop_i                        ( slv_resp_o.r_valid & slv_req_i.r_ready & slv_resp_o.r.last )
373:       );
374:     end

49: module rr_arb_tree #(
50:   /// Number of inputs to be arbitrated.
51:   parameter int unsigned NumIn      = 64,
52:   /// Data width of the payload in bits. Not needed if `DataType` is overwritten.
53:   parameter int unsigned DataWidth  = 32,
54:   /// Data type of the payload, can be overwritten with custom type. Only use of `DataWidth`.
55:   parameter type         DataType   = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
56:   /// The `ExtPrio` option allows to override the internal round robin counter via the
57:   /// `rr_i` signal. This can be useful in case multiple arbiters need to have
58:   /// rotating priorities that are operating in lock-step. If static priority arbitration
59:   /// is needed, just connect `rr_i` to '0.
60:   ///
61:   /// Set to 1'b1 to enable.
62:   parameter bit          ExtPrio    = 1'b0,
63:   /// If `AxiVldRdy` is set, the req/gnt signals are compliant with the AXI style vld/rdy
64:   /// handshake. Namely, upstream vld (req) must not depend on rdy (gnt), as it can be deasserted
65:   /// again even though vld is asserted. Enabling `AxiVldRdy` leads to a reduction of arbiter
66:   /// delay and area.
67:   ///
68:   /// Set to `1'b1` to treat req/gnt as vld/rdy.
69:   parameter bit          AxiVldRdy  = 1'b0,
70:   /// The `LockIn` option prevents the arbiter from changing the arbitration
71:   /// decision when the arbiter is disabled. I.e., the index of the first request
72:   /// that wins the arbitration will be locked in case the destination is not
73:   /// able to grant the request in the same cycle.
74:   ///
75:   /// Set to `1'b1` to enable.
76:   parameter bit          LockIn     = 1'b0,
77:   /// When set, ensures that throughput gets distributed evenly between all inputs.
78:   ///
79:   /// Set to `1'b0` to disable.
80:   parameter bit          FairArb    = 1'b1,
81:   /// Dependent parameter, do **not** overwrite.
82:   /// Width of the arbitration priority signal and the arbitrated index.
83:   parameter int unsigned IdxWidth   = (NumIn > 32'd1) ? unsigned'($clog2(NumIn)) : 32'd1,
84:   /// Dependent parameter, do **not** overwrite.
85:   /// Type for defining the arbitration priority and arbitrated index signal.
86:   parameter type         idx_t      = logic [IdxWidth-1:0]

138:     if (ExtPrio) begin : gen_ext_rr
139:       assign rr_q       = rr_i;
140:       assign req_d      = req_i;
141:     end else begin : gen_int_rr
142:       idx_t rr_d;
143: 
144:       // lock arbiter decision in case we got at least one req and no acknowledge
145:       if (LockIn) begin : gen_lock
146:         logic  lock_d, lock_q;
147:         logic [NumIn-1:0] req_q;
148: 
149:         assign lock_d     = req_o & ~gnt_i;
150:         assign req_d      = (lock_q) ? req_q : req_i;
151: 
152:         always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin : p_lock_reg
153:           if (!rst_ni) begin
154:             lock_q <= '0;
155:           end else begin
156:             if (flush_i) begin
157:               lock_q <= '0;
158:             end else begin
159:               lock_q <= lock_d;
160:             end
161:           end
162:         end
163: 
164:         `ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
165:           `ASSERT(lock, LockIn |-> req_o && (!gnt_i && !flush_i) |=> idx_o == $past(idx_o),
166:                   clk_i, !rst_ni || flush_i,
167:                   "Lock implies same arbiter decision in next cycle if output is not ready.")
168: 
169:           logic [NumIn-1:0] req_tmp;
170:           assign req_tmp = req_q & req_i;
171:           `ASSUME(lock_req, LockIn |-> lock_d |=> req_tmp == req_q, clk_i, !rst_ni || flush_i,
172:                   "It is disallowed to deassert unserved request signals when LockIn is enabled.")
173:         `endif
174: 
175:         always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin : p_req_regs
176:           if (!rst_ni) begin
177:             req_q  <= '0;
178:           end else begin
179:             if (flush_i) begin
180:               req_q  <= '0;
181:             end else begin
182:               req_q  <= req_d;
183:             end
184:           end
185:         end
186:       end else begin : gen_no_lock
187:         assign req_d = req_i;
188:       end
189: 
190:       if (FairArb) begin : gen_fair_arb
191:         logic [NumIn-1:0] upper_mask,  lower_mask;
192:         idx_t             upper_idx,   lower_idx,   next_idx;
193:         logic             upper_empty, lower_empty;
194: 
195:         for (genvar i = 0; i < NumIn; i++) begin : gen_mask
196:           assign upper_mask[i] = (i >  rr_q) ? req_d[i] : 1'b0;
197:           assign lower_mask[i] = (i <= rr_q) ? req_d[i] : 1'b0;
198:         end
199: 
200:         lzc #(
201:           .WIDTH ( NumIn ),
202:           .MODE  ( 1'b0  )
203:         ) i_lzc_upper (
204:           .in_i    ( upper_mask  ),
205:           .cnt_o   ( upper_idx   ),
206:           .empty_o ( upper_empty )
207:         );
208: 
209:         lzc #(
210:           .WIDTH ( NumIn ),
211:           .MODE  ( 1'b0  )
212:         ) i_lzc_lower (
213:           .in_i    ( lower_mask  ),
214:           .cnt_o   ( lower_idx   ),
215:           .empty_o ( /*unused*/  )
216:         );
217: 
218:         assign next_idx = upper_empty      ? lower_idx : upper_idx;
219:         assign rr_d     = (gnt_i && req_o) ? next_idx  : rr_q;
220: 
221:       end else begin : gen_unfair_arb
222:         assign rr_d = (gnt_i && req_o) ? ((rr_q == idx_t'(NumIn-1)) ? '0 : rr_q + 1'b1) : rr_q;
223:       end
224: 
225:       // this holds the highest priority
226:       always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin : p_rr_regs
227:         if (!rst_ni) begin
228:           rr_q   <= '0;
229:         end else begin
230:           if (flush_i) begin
231:             rr_q   <= '0;
232:           end else begin
233:             rr_q   <= rr_d;
234:           end
235:         end
